intro.text: AI agents now generate more tokens than humans.
So who reviews all that code?

friday.text: An AI agent just changed two hundred and thirty-seven files.
Another AI reviewed it: ninety-eight percent confident.
But the name on the approval is yours.

problems.text: An AI grading an AI shares its blind spots.

command.text: No model approves anything. Only executable evidence counts.

triage.text: First, static rules, not a model, rank the risk of every file.
Then a model that never sees the fix writes a test from the issue alone.
It must fail before, and pass after.
Outside the issue, the generated code must not change, across twenty-one cases.

crossExam.text: Then a Prosecutor, Nemotron, attacks every high-risk file.
The Defender, Gemini, can't argue: it must answer with a test that kills a broken mutant.
One by one, that took over an hour.
In parallel, every objection fans out to locked Modal sandboxes: seventeen minutes.
And most objections don't close. That's the point: you see which.

owner.text: What lands on your desk isn't two hundred files. It's twelve.
Where evidence is missing, it refuses to decide, and tells you exactly what to read.

finding.text: On another PR, the first evidence was all green.
Then cross-examination tests showed the AI fix only moved the crash.
In another run, our evidence missed it.
We logged it as an escape, and that area lost its trust.

product.text: The real report, traced to the issue.

sign.text: A sample, picked by hash, not by the AI, is read in full.
Then you sign what was checked, what wasn't, and the risk you accept.
